summary: A user-posted X report preserved in the CAM Initiative Registry shows ChatGPT being asked to rewrite prompt material while the user says “Again, do not touch image generator”; immediately below, the interface displays a Thinking/image-generation state. assessment_boundaries: The occurrence remains a single-user report and does not establish platform-wide prevalence.
The directly reviewed Registry capture supports the explicit action-scope boundary and displayed image-generation state, but not the internal routing or tool-selection implementation.

The repeated 'Again' corrective instruction, 'whenever' recurrence report and reload requirement support a provisional continuity-state interpretation, but the artefact does not fully distinguish inherited sticky state from repeated lexical re-triggering.
Capability-Authority Separation remains rejected because the artefact does not show that technical capability or tool availability was used as the material basis for permission.

Control Activation Validity remains rejected because the observed image-generation path is an action/tool-routing state, not an evidenced governance safeguard whose defined activation conditions were unsatisfied.

Control-State Preservation remains rejected because that class concerns preservation of an already-operative governance control, whereas the sticky state at issue here is the continuation validity of an interaction/tool state.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The directly reviewed Registry capture preserves the user-posted X report and embedded ChatGPT interface screenshot. The screenshot visibly shows a request to rewrite prompt material together with the corrective instruction “Again, do not touch image generator”, followed by a displayed Thinking/image-generation state. The accompanying post reports repeated triggering around the words “art”, “prompt”, and “image”, app glitch/reload behaviour, a visible switch from GPT-5.5 to “5.4 Thinking”. The partial capture does not establish the internal router, tool-selection mechanism, whether the unwanted state was inherited across turns or repeatedly re-triggered, or platform-wide prevalence. Earlier record wording included an image-upload/crash claim that is not visible in the reviewed Registry capture; that broader claim is not freshly established.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence engages both action-scope authority and continuity-state validity. First, permission to discuss or rewrite prompt text did not authorise a materially different image-generation action. Second, once the unwanted image-generation trajectory had emerged, the user's explicit corrective instruction should have invalidated or reset that trajectory for subsequent continuation. The fact that the captured interaction still enters the image-generation state, together with the report that this happened whenever relevant words were mentioned and required repeated reloads, supports a provisional Continuity-State Validity analysis. The evidence remains insufficient to claim a specific router, memory or model-state implementation. The action-scope failure is bounded to the captured interaction, with a material unresolved continuity-state clause. The occurrence is therefore partially adjudicated; it does not support a blanket system failure or invariant-held conclusion. The unresolved sticky-state versus fresh lexical-trigger distinction is preserved rather than forced into a continuity mapping. Independent standards review retains evidentiary boundaries for runtime agent-admission controls and mechanisms for overriding or repairing unwanted AI behaviour. The capture establishes unwanted tool activation but does not expose the admission policy or effective override state. Data-processing, model-development and safety-function requirements concern distinct technical objects and remain audit-only. Voluntary runtime-framework adoption is not an assessment prerequisite.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident illustrates a dual governance requirement for multimodal systems: action authority must remain bounded to the user's authorised scope, and interaction/tool state must remain validity-bounded across conversational continuation. An explicitly rejected mode should not remain governing merely because it was previously active, nor should lexical mentions silently reinstate it without renewed authority.
